title: Odds ratio as a named logit contrast
dek: OR = (p1/(1−p1))/(p0/(1−p0)). Wikipedia contrast. Not a risk ratio unless the baseline is rare. stats-logit owns the GLM.
story: An odds ratio on Wikipedia is a ratio of odds, the contrast logistic regression emits as exp(β). It is symmetric in a useful 2×2 way and invariant to case-control sampling of the intercept (under a logit).
It is not a risk ratio. At baseline risk 50%, OR=2 is a very different risk change than at baseline 1%. wiki-relative-risk is the sibling.
TB papers quoting 'twice the risk' from a logit need this card in related[].
deep: OR=1 means no association on the odds scale, not 'no important public-health effect'.
Confidence intervals for ORs are usually Wald on the log scale, then exponentiated (delta / invariance of MLE).
Adjusted ORs depend on the covariate set; they are not portable like a physical constant.
Do not average ORs from heterogeneous studies without a model (wiki-publication-bias neighbourhood).

visual.caption: Same OR=2 at two baselines. The risk ratio and risk difference move. Teaching bars, not a meta-analysis.
